Dr. Pa has more than 20 years of human neuroimaging experience, Alzheimer’s disease, mild cognitive impairment, and lifestyle factors and directs a research lab focused on factors underlying dementia prevention. This work serves our lab’s primary goal of precision prevention; to better understand which protective factors best serve who and why so we may get closer and closer to tailored interventions and treatments. One branch of Dr. Pa’s active research program focuses on developing and testing new multidomain combination interventions using technology, such as virtual reality and remote activity monitoring, with the goal of preserving brain health and cognition. Another NIH supported area of Dr. Pa’s work focuses on harmonized, big data approaches to investigate the interplay between biological sex, genetics like APOE4, and Alzheimer's disease risk factors. Read more Read more RESEARCH Research efforts in the Gur-Cohen’s lab focus on mechanisms of how epithelial stem cells are communicating with their supporting microenvironment to maintain 'stemness' identity and achieve coordinated tissue regeneration.
